Replay

Scrapyard port ledger

9 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

This ledger records port requirements, dated comparisons and remaining validation. Use the contributor guide for the current authoring workflow; individual receipts below retain their original workloads and failures.

Original repository: ../../../scrapyard, revision 6bdef4f437d9a4e2c98f1d49472f840879301ccf. Its project, source, saves and run commands remain independent. This project is a reimplementation against Replay, not a renamed Kit shell. The full Replay roadmap records the original parity scope. The later framework completion plan defers exhaustive game parity and governs the framework's release scope.

Slice Concrete requirements Status
Arena and runners Same cover generator/footprints, movement/cover slide, names/loadouts, ready/start, local prediction, remote views, camera Native/network gates; original dirt/tufts, animated gate and direction arrow restored; three-floor scene lifecycle and spectator clear-stage visibility tested
Guns and enemies Data resources, ballistic cadence/mag/reload/jam, projectiles, mobs, damage, drops All stock gun families and enemy brains implemented; baseline/native/network evidence recorded
Combat composition Abilities, statuses, combinations, chain/rail/lance/lobber/mend behavior Grenade, historical rails/healing, statuses, reaction rules and barrel chains implemented; all stock ability deliveries implemented; full original scenario parity remains pending
Run progression Waves, bosses, floors, gate, shop/workbench, wipe/reset, meta progression Run/director/gate/shop/parts/revive/reset implemented; local co-op profiles implemented; inspector-driven workbench previews tested; audio/settings and spray preview implemented; complete listening/visual parity pending
Recovery and identity Drop-in/reconnect, spectator/server parity, saves, host migration during combat, returned host Local profiles, saves, party menus/durable enrollment, and asset-aware combat handoff/rejoin tested; full recovery/identity matrix pending
Stress and content Zones, delivery/storm/surge/healing, gauntlet, spray/mod content, audio/UI polish Zone/delivery/healing, cross-seat storm/surge, continuous three-wave/barrel finale and fault gates; spray exchange/recovery, host-only JSON overlays and 40-enemy stress tested; matched solo waves and cover-aware finales pass in eight required games plus a reversed obstruction control; difficulty comparison and polish pending
Deployment/comparison Web/Steam paths, matched old/new acts, measurements and human playtests Local Chrome party enrollment/asset-aware migration, world equality, profiles/run/spray persistence pass; optimized paired idle and firing/reload comparisons pass; public deployment, Steam, full combat comparisons and human playtests pending

The original harness acts map to the new implementation as follows. “Pending” identifies an unmet item in that original parity scope. It does not claim an intentional gameplay difference, and it does not independently block the revised framework release scope.

Original act Replay acceptance
duo / solo / server Dedicated server act now passes in both isolated games: two clients, six-enemy clear, rewards and floor advance with no authority avatar; broader mode/movement parity pending
guns Ballistic families, cadence, magazine/reload/jam, mob hits and drops
combo / lance Data-driven effects, directional/time queries and cross-entity effects
run / boss / gauntlet Complete progression/director state and sustained play
vault / doppelganger Durable profiles tested; duplicate live identity policy differs (see below)
succession Complete checkpoint, fenced takeover, recorded 150-tick timer reset; native/Chrome dedicated combat planned/crash continuation passes; broader matrix pending
stress Matched entity/shot workload and CPU/memory/bandwidth measurements
spray / mod Asset transfer, declared content compatibility and late join
chain / delivery / zone Deferred multi-entity consequences and lifetime
storm / surge / mend Area/status/healing behavior and attribution

The dedicated-server increment compares the original server act in separate projects and fixes avatarless Room bootstrap/standby/takeover. Native planned, crash/return and repeated infrastructure failover preserve both real player seats and exact checkpoint frames. The browser infrastructure gate now exercises those role transitions in four real Chrome processes over RTC. Dedicated combat-failover and broader deployment remain open.

The network recording increment adds developer-menu exports and a headless verifier for complete network batches. Real native authority/prediction and Chrome solo recordings execute in native/WASM, including accepted/rejected actions and historical aim. It preserves gameplay and recovery formats; it is an explicit diagnostic with measured synchronous cost, not a full-game parity or adoption result.

Current comparison boundaries:

  • The cover-aware solo cohort passes normal stopping positions and a deterministic blocked-shot control using ordinary movement. Barrels, cover, damage and all wave/rest/reward requirements remain. It is a new controller contract; the older stationary result below stays rejected and is not a difficulty or human-feel verdict.

  • The solo gauntlet comparison runs one circle-strafing player with nearest-target autofire in both real games. All six fresh-profile games clear 4/4/5 enemies, retain all three 300-tick rests, and award one core. Five complete the barrel chain; one Replay stopping position leaves both fixed-offset barrels behind cover. That failure is retained, and the overall cohort is rejected. This is sustained solo evidence, with differing health/timing observations, not difficulty or human-feel equivalence.

  • The action-intent helper replaces manual dash ticket storage, preserves input guards and handles recovery dispositions across epoch changes. Native input, party and live request checks pass; the source-count reduction is not a human usability or performance claim.

  • The snapshot-ACK comparison passes Replay's twelve delay/raw-loss windows and paired delay acceptance with 61 report cases. The paired raw-loss scope still fails a Kit client observation; Replay's observed-state gaps reach 1.369 seconds. Controlled ENet and core tests verify the removed ACK/action blocking dependency.

  • The stress-aim correction uses the predicted local origin with the observed enemy census. Native regression and impact-ledger checks pass; the fresh delay condition passes twelve windows and 61 report cases. Raw loss still fails a client battlecry observation, and a separate diagnostic records a cooldown refusal caused by bunched arrivals.

  • The dash-action port uses receipt-time dash intents and explicit results, with content 42–46 conversion and native input/save/model plus WASM-build validation. All 120 local dash requests in the new cohort settle, including raw-loss cases. The paired workload still fails minimum kill counts in three Replay games; observation freshness and broader authoring/platform/human validation remain open. The current-content native TLS party handoff/asset-recovery/returned-host gate also passes; a fresh browser party run after this content change remains pending.

  • The jam-clearing comparison passes twelve delay windows and 60 report cases, including seeded duds, live shots, three-pull clears and settled gun-state convergence. Raw-loss acceptance remains failed for stale Kit cooldown observations and a lost Replay dash.

  • The latest endurance cohort passes delay and raw-loss conditions with 24 windows and 56 report cases. Prior failures remain recorded; long observation gaps and broader injury/jam/wave, platform and human-playtest coverage remain open.

  • Cast submission measurement now distinguishes Kit local prediction rejection from a sent request. The prior refusal diagnosis was incorrect; current raw-loss workload failures remain recorded and still prevent full paired acceptance.

  • The endurance comparison adds stock reloads, dash inputs and burn/salve/surge during the moving swarm. The delay condition passes, using an explicit Receipt action policy only in the isolated Replay copy. Raw-loss acceptance fails for missing remote dash edges; the subsequent input audit fixes Replay capture across catch-up, while the latest paired raw-loss gate remains rejected for a Kit-side cast refusal. This is not full combat/fault parity or an adoption result.

  • Cover generation and ordered axis collision are compared against selected unmodified original procedures, compiled in an isolated native oracle. The independent project does not run the original harness or touch its user data.

  • Ordinary movement preserves the original non-normalized per-axis input rule. Replay schedules movement at 60 Hz with server authority and local prediction; the original streams owner-local movement at render cadence. Network authority and variable-frame timing are therefore not matched yet.

  • Dash uses ten simulation ticks and a 66-tick cooldown. The original specifies 0.16 s / 1.1 s on the owner clock. These require paired feel/timing evaluation.

  • The renderer includes original runner strips, weapon regions, ground, solid junk, dirt/tufts and animated gate/arrow. Scenery evidence covers three peers/floors and visual captures. The bottom shop cards replace the tall overlay, restore the original purchase-key order and validate clicks/shortcuts through the same action path. The combat HUD restores health/status/cooldown displays, magazine states, boss health and revive prompts. Run transitions add departure/wipe panels, current wave/rest information and recovery narration. The downed-player camera now follows a living teammate and handles revival, host loss and rendered floor warps. Chat/system history now includes named text, late-join history, per-tick yard announcements and asset-aware migration. Positional pings restore middle-mouse input, fading markers and stamped names with expiry and floor/run scope checks. Named observer chat now passes native and browser checks, including planned host migration and retained historical labels. Broader observer/actor/menu/interaction parity remains work. Browser UI acceptance covers chat, pings, shop, HUD and camera/revival in three Chrome processes; broader browser/device and presentation coverage remains required. Audio is implemented, but hardware playback and listening parity remain unverified; the local CoreAudio path stalls even in plain Godot.

  • Actor presentation now covers downed poses/beacons, muzzle and reload cues, ghost tint, hit feedback, enemy attack/death rows and pooled slot reuse. Combat feedback supplies bounded bursts/debris, target damage numbers and pickup effects. The Escape menu/tally now adds dimming, responsive panels, healing credit, keyboard focus guards and Quit. Staging muster now restores fixed idle previews, readiness rows, bidirectional pickers and late Drop In. Automatic loadouts now preserve choice modes across native/browser restarts and seat changes. The tally now includes the original zero-valued deaths column and fresh session round-trip measurements; remaining actor/front-door details still need work. Screen effects restore lens kicks, health vignette and transition veil with motion-setting and native/browser validation.

  • Directional wounds now use the hit origin and recorded victim pose, reject stale generations/history and correct hurt burst/sound placement. Wall contacts now preserve ballistic/spit endpoints and normals, with bounded confirmed sparks, sound and content-45 save conversion. Ordnance presentation extends contact facts to rails and restores grenade shells and confirmed ember trails; bounce/fuse laws are unchanged. Glob discs restore slime/sparkjar/spit shapes, colors and pulse. The original has straight-moving discs, correcting the earlier arc/trail claim. Area effects restore filled nova/reaction/blast discs, standing zones and buff bursts. Cast paths now restore local/remote tongues and recorded spread bolts, with explicit content-46 conversion. Remaining launch/contact feedback and paired timing/feel still need work.

  • All stock gun/mob resources load into a validated value catalog carried by the host world. Ballistic guns, melee enemies, damage and pickups now run in the simulation; combat.md records timing, ordering, capacity and presentation differences. PNG spray transfer is implemented; host-only JSON overlays now ship through the world catalog.

Before claiming full parity, every row needs its real-process scenario, source/content fingerprints, recovery cases where relevant, and visual/playtest evidence. Initial movement gates do not establish full-game completion or framework superiority.

Identity policy under review: the original doppelganger act assigns a live duplicate token a fresh seat. Replay currently rejects a duplicate live identity, preserving one token-to-seat binding and requiring a separate identity for a second player. The user has been asked whether the new game should retain that rule or create a fresh guest identity for the duplicate. This row is not an agreed parity waiver.

The content-49 succession result reproduces the original attack/director timer reset on the first committed takeover tick. Exact restore, replay, repeated pending recovery, active boss/popper damage, nine old-save Godot resumes, and native/Chrome dedicated combat continuation pass. Complete projectile/lob/zone preservation remains Replay behavior; the original clears some transient pools. This does not close full gameplay/identity parity or the broader recovery/deployment matrix.
